algorithm.byte_order: no multi-byte integer: every length and code is one byte
algorithm.layout: AcceptedV2: tag:u8=1 || message_id:16 || resolved_endpoint_len:u8 (1..64) || resolved_destination_endpoint; RejectedV2: tag:u8=2 || message_id:16 || reason:u8
notes: resolved_endpoint_len is never 0: the field names the endpoint that took the message, the default already resolved.

reason numbers schemas/direct/reject-reason's enum in order from 1: no_route 1, unauthorized_peer 2, overloaded 3, malformed 4, too_large 5, shutting_down 6, unsupported 7. 0 and 8..255 are unassigned and refused as malformed, never read as unsupported.
Any other tag, a short field, or a byte after the last field is malformed response metadata.

$comment: Vectors are DERIVED from the layout in DIRECT.md §Response byte layout; no ADR publishes a golden response, so the file is anchored by its `adr` list, as direct-message-v2-frame.json is. Every assigned reason code has a vector, because the numbering is the part a second implementation would otherwise have to guess. No `contract` URN: the frame is a byte layout JSON Schema cannot express; the reason vocabulary it numbers is urn:interweave:schemas:direct:reject-reason.

vectors.name: accepted-claude
vectors.description: The ordinary acceptance: the explicit destination `claude` took the message, echoed with the request's id.

vectors.name: accepted-max-label-64
vectors.description: The longest legal response, 82 bytes: a 64-byte resolved endpoint.

vectors.name: rejected-no-route
vectors.description: Reason code 1. The one the privacy collapse rides on: endpoint unknown, disabled, unleased, no default, and endpoint-policy denial all answer this.
